concept.name: Data Quality Checks

relationships.description: Connects Data Quality Checks to data warehousing lakehouse in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Data quality checks validate schema, freshness, volume, distribution, and business invariants across ingestion and transformation stages so corrupted data is quarantined before reaching dashboards or ML models.
spark.keyTakeaway: Shift data quality left into CI/CD and ingestion contracts, and pair deterministic rule assertions with statistical anomaly detection and circuit-breaker quarantining.

concept.whyItMatters: Silent data corruption—such as a timezone shift, nullified join key, or duplicate Kafka consumer offset—erodes executive trust, trains broken ML models, and triggers costly regulatory or billing errors long before an infrastructure alert fires.
whenToUse: At ingestion boundaries (Bronze/Raw) to enforce schemas, non-null primary keys, and freshness SLAs via data contracts.
Inside transformation pipelines (dbt, Spark) using Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) before promoting tables to production.
On critical downstream metrics and ML feature stores where silent distribution drift degrades model accuracy.
whenNotToUse: Running heavy full-table statistical profiling on every micro-batch (e.g., 10-second streaming windows) where it adds unacceptable latency.
Applying rigid static thresholds (e.g., row_count == 10000) to organically growing or seasonal traffic without dynamic bounds.
Duplicating identical checks across 5 pipeline stages without clear ownership or actionable alerting.
keyPoints: Five core dimensions: completeness (null rates), uniqueness (duplicate keys), validity (regex/enum/range), timeliness (freshness lag), and consistency (referential integrity).
Deterministic vs. probabilistic checks: use hard assertions (`amount >= 0`, `pk_unique`) for invariants and statistical checks (z-score, PSI, seasonal EWMA) for volume and distribution drift.
Write-Audit-Publish (WAP): stage new data in an isolated branch or snapshot (e.g., Iceberg branch / Nessie), run quality gates, and atomically fast-forward production only on pass.
Severity tiering: route blocking failures (`ERROR`) to quarantine/DLQ and halt promotion, while routing soft drift (`WARN`) to Slack/observability without breaking SLAs.
Contract-first enforcement: validate producer payloads at the Kafka Schema Registry or API gateway before malformed records enter the lakehouse.

examples.title: Write-Audit-Publish on Daily Billing Mart
examples.scenario: A SaaS billing pipeline occasionally ingested duplicate Stripe webhook events, inflating daily ARR reports by 8% until finance caught it manually at month-end.
examples.outcome: The team implemented WAP on Apache Iceberg using dbt tests (`unique` on `invoice_id`, `not_null`, and a custom SQL invariant checking `net_amount == gross - discount`). Failed runs stay on the staging branch and page on-call, reducing billing discrepancies to zero.

examples.title: ML Feature Drift Detection in Fraud Scoring
examples.scenario: An upstream mobile SDK update accidentally changed `device_os_version` from `17.2` to `iOS 17.2`, causing a fraud model's categorical encoder to default to `UNKNOWN` and spike false declines by 3.4%.
examples.outcome: Adding Soda Core distribution checks (categorical set membership + Population Stability Index > 0.2) caught the schema-valid semantic drift within 15 minutes of deployment.

tradeOffs.factor: Strict Circuit Breaking vs. Data Freshness
tradeOffs.pro: Halting publication on failed checks guarantees downstream consumers never see corrupted numbers.
tradeOffs.con: False-positive alerts or minor non-critical column nulls can freeze entire executive dashboards during peak hours.

tradeOffs.factor: Full-Table Scans vs. Incremental Partition Checks
tradeOffs.pro: Full-table checks catch cross-partition duplicates and global referential integrity violations.
tradeOffs.con: Scanning multi-terabyte Iceberg/BigQuery tables on every run explodes compute costs; partition-scoped checks are 10–100x cheaper.

tradeOffs.factor: Static Rules vs. ML Anomaly Detection
tradeOffs.pro: Static rules (`price > 0`) are deterministic, explainable, and have zero false positives.
tradeOffs.con: Static rules miss subtle volume drops (e.g., 40% drop in EU traffic) that adaptive time-series baselines detect automatically.

failureModes.name: Alert Fatigue from Noisy Thresholds
failureModes.description: Teams configure dozens of uncalibrated `WARN` checks on volatile columns, causing engineers to mute the Slack channel and miss real outages.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce strict severity tiers: only page on Tier-1 contract invariants; calibrate statistical bounds using 28-day seasonal baselines.

failureModes.name: Check-After-Publish Race Condition
failureModes.description: Quality tests run asynchronously after the production table is overwritten, meaning BI tools and ML jobs already consumed bad data.
failureModes.mitigation: Adopt the Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) pattern using Iceberg/Delta branching or blue-green table swaps.

failureModes.name: Quarantine Black Hole
failureModes.description: Invalid records are routed to a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) or quarantine table that nobody monitors or replays, causing silent data loss.
failureModes.mitigation: Track DLQ volume as an SLI with an alert when > 0.1% of records are quarantined, and automate replay scripts after schema fixes.

failureModes.name: Unbounded Scan Cost Explosion
failureModes.description: Unpartitioned `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)` or regex checks run hourly across 5 years of history, spiking Snowflake/BigQuery spend.
failureModes.mitigation: Scope checks to the incremental partition (`WHERE event_date = CURRENT_DATE`) and use approximate sketches (HyperLogLog) for cardinality.

commonMistakes: Testing only for NULLs and data types while ignoring business invariants (e.g., `refund_amount <= order_total` or `ship_date >= order_date`).
Running data quality checks only in production instead of executing unit/contract tests in CI on synthetic or sampled staging data.
Treating row-count > 0 as sufficient validation, which misses silent 50% drops or duplicate-row inflation.
Writing custom one-off Python validation scripts per pipeline instead of declarative frameworks (dbt tests, Soda, Great Expectations, SQLMesh audits).
Failing to attach lineage and owner metadata to quality alerts, leaving responders guessing which upstream microservice broke.

sections.content:
## The idea

Data quality checks are automated assertions and statistical monitors placed at key boundaries of a data pipeline to verify that datasets are **fit for purpose** before consumers rely on them.

A mature quality architecture separates **structural/contract checks** (schema, types, non-null keys, enum values), **semantic/business invariants** (balance equations, state transitions, referential integrity), and **observability/drift checks** (freshness lag, volume anomalies, distribution shifts). Rather than fixing corrupted tables after dashboards break, modern pipelines combine **shift-left contracts** at ingestion with **Write-Audit-Publish (WAP)** gates during transformation.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider an hourly **Clickstream & Revenue** pipeline loading events into an Apache Iceberg table:

1. **Ingestion Gate (Kafka + Schema Registry)**: Producers serialize events in Avro. Malformed payloads missing `event_id` or `timestamp_utc` are rejected at the producer or routed to `events.dlq`.
2. **Write Stage (Isolated Branch)**: Spark reads the hourly Kafka micro-batch and writes transformed records to an isolated Iceberg branch `audit_2026_11_12_10`—invisible to BI users querying `main`.
3. **Audit Stage (Soda / dbt / SQLMesh)**: Automated checks run on the branch:
   - `unique(event_id)` and `not_null(user_id, revenue_usd)`
   - `revenue_usd >= 0 AND revenue_usd < 100000`
   - `row_count` within 3 standard deviations of the same hour over the past 4 weeks.
4. **Publish or Quarantine**: If all `ERROR`-tier checks pass, Iceberg atomically fast-forwards `main` to the audited snapshot. If a check fails, `main` remains untouched, the bad batch stays in `audit_*` for inspection, and PagerDuty alerts the owning domain.

sections.content:
## Deterministic rules vs. statistical observability

Relying solely on one style leaves blind spots:

- **Deterministic Assertions**: Explicit SQL/Python rules (`not_null`, `accepted_values`, `relationships`, `expression_is_true`). Ideal for primary keys, currency codes, and accounting identities (`assets == liabilities + equity`). Zero ambiguity, fast to execute on incremental partitions.
- **Statistical Observability**: Automated profiling of metadata and distributions over time—freshness (time since last commit), volume (row count z-score / Prophet seasonality), and distribution drift (KL-divergence, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, PSI). Essential for catching upstream bugs that remain schema-valid (e.g., an ad campaign tracker dropping UTM parameters for Safari users).

## Comparison of data quality tooling

| Tool / Pattern | Execution Layer | Primary Strength | Best For | Key Limitation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **dbt / SQLMesh Audits** | Warehouse SQL (Snowflake, BigQuery, Trino) | Tightly coupled with SQL models & Git CI | Transformation-layer invariants & WAP | Limited statistical/ML drift detection |
| **Soda Core / SodaCL** | SQL & Spark DataFrames | Human-readable YAML checks & anomaly detection | Cross-team contracts & freshness SLAs | Advanced observability features require cloud tier |
| **Great Expectations** | Python / Spark / SQL | Rich library of 50+ built-in statistical expectations | Complex Python/Spark data engineering pipelines | Verbose configuration & higher boilerplate |
| **Schema Registry + DLQ** | Kafka / Pulsar / API Gateway | Prevents malformed records at the source | Real-time event streams & microservices | Validates single-record syntax, not cross-row aggregates |
| **Monte Carlo / Elementary** | Metadata & Query Logs | Zero-config freshness, volume & lineage alerts | Broad warehouse monitoring across 1,000+ tables | Can miss domain-specific business logic bugs |

## Failure modes

- **Silent Schema Evolution**: Adding a nullable column or changing an enum value upstream causes downstream `CASE WHEN` statements to fall into `ELSE NULL` without raising an error.
- **Late-Arriving Data False Positives**: Mobile clients offline for 48 hours flush batched events, triggering volume spike alerts or failing `event_timestamp >= partition_date` checks.
- **Quarantine Accumulation**: Routing bad rows to a DLQ without retention policies or replay automation turns the DLQ into an unmonitored graveyard of lost revenue events.
- **Test Suite Drift**: Engineers disable failing dbt tests (`severity: warn` or `# skip`) during an incident and never re-enable them.

sections.eyebrow: 06 / Production patterns: quarantine, backfill, and SLIs
sections.content:
## Production patterns: quarantine, backfill, and SLIs

1. **Row-Level Quarantine vs. Batch Halt**: For non-critical dimensions (e.g., optional user survey fields), tag bad rows with `_dq_error_reason` and route them to a quarantine table while letting valid rows proceed. For financial ledgers, halt the entire batch.
2. **Partition-Scoped Incremental Audits**: Always filter checks by `_ingested_at >= window_start` or Iceberg snapshot diffs (`SELECT * FROM table.changes`) to keep audit latency under 30 seconds.
3. **Quality SLIs**: Track **Bad Record Rate** (`quarantined_rows / total_rows`), **Time-to-Detect (TTD)**, and **Freshness SLO Attainment** per data product.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Enforce schema contracts (Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema) at ingestion boundaries with a monitored DLQ.
- [ ] Implement Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) on Tier-1 tables so unverified data is never visible on `main`.
- [ ] Cover all 5 dimensions: completeness, uniqueness, validity, freshness, and business invariants.
- [ ] Scope audit queries to incremental partitions or snapshot deltas to control warehouse compute costs.
- [ ] Separate `ERROR` (blocking/paging) from `WARN` (observability/Slack) to eliminate alert fatigue.

interviewProblems.title: Data Quality Checks
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Data Quality Checks. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Data quality checks validate schema, freshness, volume, distribution, and business invariants across ingestion and transformation stages so corrupted data is quarantined before reaching dashboards or ML models.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Quality Engine applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Production Table.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Production Table experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Enforce strict severity tiers: only page on Tier-1 contract invariants; calibrate statistical bounds using 28-day seasonal baselines.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Shift data quality left into CI/CD and ingestion contracts, and pair deterministic rule assertions with statistical anomaly detection and circuit-breaker quarantining.
Avoid trap: Testing only for NULLs and data types while ignoring business invariants (e.g., `refund_amount <= order_total` or `ship_date >= order_date`).
Avoid trap: Running data quality checks only in production instead of executing unit/contract tests in CI on synthetic or sampled staging data.
When to reach for it: At ingestion boundaries (Bronze/Raw) to enforce schemas, non-null primary keys, and freshness SLAs via data contracts.
When to reach for it: Inside transformation pipelines (dbt, Spark) using Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) before promoting tables to production.

putItTogether.title: Putting Data Quality Checks Together
putItTogether.summary: Shift data quality left into CI/CD and ingestion contracts, and pair deterministic rule assertions with statistical anomaly detection and circuit-breaker quarantining.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Data Quality Checks before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: The team implemented WAP on Apache Iceberg using dbt tests (`unique` on `invoice_id`, `not_null`, and a custom SQL invariant checking `net_amount == gross - discount`). Failed runs stay on the staging branch and page on-call, reducing billing discrepancies to zero.
